submitter: bugs_open/381 lane — the site planner composes pages from components that cannot express what the page promises
rationale:
WHAT IS BROKEN. A page's own heading promises a month-by-month calendar and the page ships four prose blocks. On garden-tools.uk the seasonal-planner page was composed of hero + generic-text-block + info-card-grid + call-to-action, NONE of which can render a list, so the writer had nowhere to put twelve months and wrote four seasons of prose. Nothing downstream reports it: the sections rendered, the page deployed, every check passed. [MEASURED 2026-08-24, fleet 30d] 741 pages across 29 sites; 327 (44%) contain no list, no table and no anywhere in their content; 1,863 of 1,980 section placements (94%) used a template that cannot produce a list or a table. THE CAUSE IS IN TWO PLACES AND THIS SUBMISSION FIXES BOTH. (A) The planner's component menu prints name/display_name/function/description and NOTHING about what markup a component can produce, so it chooses blind on expressiveness. Three live planners share that shape. (B) The writer's rulebook has exactly two sentences about markup, and between them they instruct every prose slot into paragraphs. RULE 9: 'For fields of type text: return a plain string with no HTML wrapping.' RULE 10 permits

, and only for types rich_text/content — which [MEASURED 2026-08-24] ZERO components declare (940 llm fields are text, 2 are html). The only rule permitting structure is addressed to nobody. THE LEVER IS llm_guidance, NOT THE DECLARED TYPE, AND THIS CORRECTS THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS FIX. A controlled comparison already exists in the estate with the type held constant [MEASURED 2026-08-24, 30d instances]: article-body.content is type text, HAS llm_guidance asking for headings and lists, and renders a list in 116/153 = 76% of instances. generic-text-block.content is type text, has NO llm_guidance at all, and renders a list in 12/173 = 7%. Same type, same renderer, same RULE 9 — eleven-fold difference. So RULE 9 does not bind and the field's own guidance does. My first plan had this backwards (retype and the writer is freed); article-body is the disproof. The retype to html keeps a smaller and honest job: the prompt prints each field as `content (TYPE, required)` and its rules are addressed BY TYPE, so the type is the ROUTING KEY between RULE 9 and RULE 10. WHY CAPABILITY IS DERIVED AND NOT DECLARED. content_components.content_shape already exists for exactly this purpose (COMMENT: 'prose, structured_list, structured_card, key_value_pairs'). It is DEAD: zero Go readers repo-wide, omitted from the birth INSERT (store_generated_component_action.go:634 sets 19 columns and not this one), NULL on 128 of 151 active section rows, drifted to free text (series, sequence, mixed), and 12 rows marked structured_list have no list markup in their template. A hand-maintained capability column IS the failure mode being fixed. So component_expresses() is IMMUTABLE and called at READ time from the menu queries: no ALTER TABLE, no trigger, nothing to backfill, nothing to go stale when the RFC_032/bugs_open/283 lane rewrites html_template fleet-wide (140 of 297 active templates now carry the InstanceID token). WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO. It adds no component. Enumerated 2026-08-24, the 44 structural components are directories, trackers, calculators, quizzes, spec sheets, one pricing table, two carousels and site-footer (chrome) — there is NO generic checklist, steps, comparison-table or calendar component. So (A) converts a blind choice into an informed one; it cannot make a seasonal planner possible. That gap is recorded in bugs_open/381 as a finding, not smuggled in here. It also changes no Go, rewrites no existing page, and touches no html_template. TIMING RISK ACCEPTED AND STATED. The 305 lane's define-by-negation scanner splits sentences on ) and nothing here is unsafe alone.

plan.summary: bugs_open/381: derive what each component can EXPRESS from its own template and schema, print it in all three planner menus with a rule that ties structure to promise, and give the four pass-through prose slots the field guidance that measurably produces structure (article-body 76% vs generic-text-block 7%) — retyping them to html so the writer's RULE 10 is addressed to a type that exists. Five config-only migrations, live on apply, no chassis roll, each with a refusing rollback sidecar. All five applied and rolled back against the live DB inside one transaction; every guard mutation-proven to refuse, with controls proving they still admit the real thing.

edits.rationale: The vocabulary, derived not declared: html-block (an llm field typed html), list (literal <ul/<ol), table (literal <table), items (a range over an llm array field), empty = prose only. IMMUTABLE, called from the menu SELECT so nothing is stored or backfilled — deliberate, because the 283 lane is rewriting html_template fleet-wide and a stored capability would be stale the moment a template changed. The menu gains one column; the listing line gains an [expresses: ...] / [prose only] token; rule 19 tells the planner that a page promising a calendar, steps, a checklist, a comparison or a specification needs a section that expresses list/table/items/html-block. The evidence-base row gate mirrors 419's requires-backend clause so a fact-fed component is not surfaced as a generic list-expresser on a site with no evidence base; NO row carries that tag today, so the clause is inert on apply and changes no menu by one row — deliberate, the semantics should exist before the tags.
edits.sketch:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION component_expresses(p_html_template text, p_input_schema jsonb) RETURNS text[] LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE AS $fn$
  SELECT COALESCE(array_agg(x ORDER BY x), ARRAY[]::text[]) FROM (
    SELECT 'html-block'::text AS x WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM jsonb_each(COALESCE(p_input_schema->'fields','{}'::jsonb)) f WHERE f.value->>'source'='llm' AND f.value->>'type'='html')
    UNION SELECT 'list'  WHERE p_html_template ~* '<(ul|ol)[\s>]' OR EXISTS (... type='html')
    UNION SELECT 'table' WHERE p_html_template ~* '<table[\s>]'  OR EXISTS (... type='html')
    UNION SELECT 'items' WHERE p_html_template ~* '\{\{[-\s]*range' AND EXISTS (... type IN ('array','list'))
  ) s; $fn$;

-- menu SELECT gains: , array_to_string(component_expresses(html_template, input_schema), ', ') AS expresses
-- listing line gains: {{if .expresses}} [expresses: {{.expresses}}]{{else}} [prose only]{{end}}
-- guards: exactly 1 live row; menu SELECT verbatim; 419's requires-backend clause present; listing line exactly once; 'Return ONLY valid JSON.' exactly once; not already applied
-- verify includes a NEGATIVE control: component_expresses(call-to-action) must be empty, because a control that matches everything is not a control

edits.rationale: Same remedy for the second planner; guards on component_expresses existing and refuses without 591. NO evidence-base gate here, and the header states it as a known hole rather than papering over it: this menu query takes no site parameter, so the gate cannot be expressed without inventing one and threading a site id the workflow does not carry at that step. Small today — site-planner ran 5 times in the 30 days to 2026-08-24 against content-gap-planner's 749 — and closing it is a separate change with its own blast radius.

BY VOLUME THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST: [MEASURED 2026-08-24, llm_call_log 30d] content-gap-planner 749 calls, build-site-planner 27, site-planner 5. The bug was found on a greenfield build but most component choices on this estate are made here. This prompt carries a prefix-cache breakpoint and the components listing sits INSIDE the cached prefix (listing at char 853, breakpoint at 897), so both edits invalidate that prefix once per site. Stated, not hidden: the menu is already site-varying (its query binds $1) so the prefix was never shared across sites in the first place. The marker is not moved, duplicated or fragmented, and the verify block asserts it still appears exactly once AND still follows the components block — a fragmented prefix is the failure mode migration 377 exists to prevent.
edits.sketch:
IF (length(p)-length(replace(p,'<!--CACHE_BREAKPOINT-->','')))/length('<!--CACHE_BREAKPOINT-->') <> 1 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION '593: expected exactly one cache breakpoint marker — the prefix contract has changed, refusing'; END IF;
IF position('## Available Section Components' in p) > position('<!--CACHE_BREAKPOINT-->' in p) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION '593 VERIFY: the components block has moved past the cache breakpoint'; END IF;

edits.symbol: content_components.input_schema for generic-text-block.content, about-content.content, illustrated-text-block.content, article-body.content
edits.rationale:
THE MEASURED HALF. generic-text-block and about-content have NO guidance today; illustrated-text-block's guidance actively restricts it to '

paragraphs'; article-body's guidance already works (76%) and is NOT rewritten — only the forbidden-elements sentence is appended, and

stays permitted there alone because that component IS a whole article body rather than a section slot. FOUR FIELDS NOT FIVE: report-dossier.body matched the structural census predicate and is EXCLUDED because its own guidance says it is never authored by an LLM — only the guidance text distinguishes it, the structural predicate cannot, and that is recorded. The guidance forbids /

RULE 10 is re-addressed from rich_text/content (declared by zero components) to html, and says what structure means: <h3> on a turn, <ul>/<ol> where genuinely enumerable, <strong> for the scanned term, <table> only when tabular — plus an explicit do-not-pad clause. RULE 9 is NARROWED, not weakened: 304's markdown ban stays absolute and is restated, and the verify block asserts it SURVIVED the replace. What RULE 9 stops asserting is that a text field may never contain markup, because that was already false in practice — article-body is text, is asked for lists, and produces them 76% of the time — so the rulebook is made to match what the estate already does rather than the reverse. Examples are deliberately NOT first-person practice claims (the months of the year, the steps a reader takes, the options being compared — never 'our testing process, step by step'), coordinated with the bugs_open/380 lane whose writer arm forbids exactly that shape on a site with no operating history. 304's rollback will REFUSE after this file, by design: it guards on the literal this replaces, so it declines rather than mis-splicing, and 595's own rollback restores both rules verbatim.
edits.sketch:
-- pre-state: rule 9 exactly once verbatim, rule 10 exactly once verbatim, 304's markdown ban present, not already applied
replace(replace(tpl,
  $old10$10. For fields of type `rich_text` or `content` that contain multiple paragraphs: ...$old10$,
  $new10$10. For fields of type `html`: write real structure, not a run of paragraphs. ... Do NOT pad to earn a list: if the material is one idea, one paragraph is the right answer, and a three-item list of near-identical clauses is worse than the paragraph it replaced. ... Where this field's own description gives more specific guidance, that description wins.$new10$),
  $old9$9. For fields of type `text`: return a plain string with no HTML wrapping. The template handles paragraph wrapping for these fields.$old9$,
  $new9$9. For fields of type `text`: return a plain string — a heading, a label, a sentence — with no HTML wrapping around it. ... If this field's own description asks for particular markup inside it, follow the description: it knows what its slot renders.$new9$)

-- VERIFY: 304's markdown ban survived; rich_text no longer named; rules in order; three unrelated landmarks still present so this file provably touched only rules 9 and 10

plan.risks:
1. THE CENTRAL EMPIRICAL RISK: the 76%-vs-7% comparison is observational, not an experiment, and it is confounded by WHO writes each field — article-body is written on the blog path, generic-text-block by page-content-writer. If the writer PROMPT rather than the field GUIDANCE is what actually differs between them, 594's guidance will not move generic-text-block toward 76%. This is written into the lane's PLAN as its own falsifier and is exactly what the acceptance measure tests. 595 hedges it by fixing the prompt half too, so the two arms fail independently rather than together.
2. Prompt-token cost. The listing gains a short token per component across 149-151 rows on three planners, and 593's edit invalidates a cached prefix once per site. Measured position, not estimated. Not free — and the alternative (a per-section brief, PLAN-025) is materially larger, which is why it is deferred rather than bundled here.
3. The evidence-base gate is INERT on apply: no row carries requires-evidence-base yet, and the tagging UPDATE is owed by the editorial_design_uplift lane, whose session is blocked on its own permission gate. An untagged row is ungated-as-today, so this is safe in either order, but until they land it the protection is nominal rather than real. Stated rather than implied.
4. site-planner gets no evidence gate at all, because its menu query has no site parameter. A real, named hole; 5 calls in 30 days.
5. A writer told to use lists may pad. Mitigated in the words themselves (do NOT pad to earn a list; a three-item list of near-identical clauses is worse than the paragraph it replaced) and detectable in the acceptance measure as a rise in list count with no rise in quality — but a prompt instruction is not a control on output and I am not claiming it is.
6. Timing: 595 should preferably land after the next chassis roll so the 305 lane's </th sentence-boundary fix is live. Narrow exposure (needs a define-by-negation construction inside a table header cell); nothing here is unsafe alone.
7. Rollback asymmetry in 594 is deliberate and could confuse a future reader: two fields had no llm_guidance key (it is REMOVED on rollback), one had specific wording (restored verbatim), one is append-only (the appended sentence is stripped). The sidecar's header states this.
